author: Claude Sonnet/high
finding_scope_note: R1/R2 are generic hardening defects demonstrated with synthetic hash-rebound in-memory inputs, not original hash-chain bypasses or errors in the exact committed snapshot.

findings.detail: commit_oid is validated only as str. Empty, invalid, or nonexistent commits enter commit_to_paths and never correlate. A simulated validator drift then leaves code.mapping_exact_commit_review RETAINED without a code dependency. Removing only injected_runtime from a nonempty observation map promotes the already-drifted slice-3 row to RETAINED. Reject malformed/unresolvable observations and require complete reviewed dependency coverage before retaining a code review.
findings.title: Unresolved or incomplete observations silently remove required dependency checks

findings.detail: The selected dependency is artifacts[obs_path], verified at artifacts[path].git_commit, not at obs.commit_oid. Observation sha256/tree_oid are ignored. Rebinding the runtime artifact to valid current HEAD bytes while retaining its older observation and review terminal falsely retains slice-3. Swapping the validator observation path to the existing ledgers path similarly retains a drifted validator. Verify each observation path at its own commit/tree/hash and compare current bytes to that baseline; preserve commit/path identity in dependency references.
findings.title: Observation commit is used for correlation but not for the byte baseline

findings.detail: code.launch_validator_commit_tree also cites the mapping terminal candidate_commit, making three correlated identities. It already directly lists validator source and remains FUTURE, so this has no classification impact. The snapshot also adds ledger and runtime source_refs to slice-3, beyond its stated remaining_obligation change. Correct the handoff.
findings.title: Handoff overstates its exhaustive correlation and difference checks
